plants.name: Wisteria sinensis
plants.description: Woody vines hang heavy chains of fragrant, pea-like blue-violet flowers. The blooms open in 15–30 cm clusters, often before the leaves fully unfurl. They drape pergolas, walls and old trees in a lilac-purple cascade.
plants.location: Native to China; widely grown in temperate gardens, with Japan's famous wisteria parks peaking from late April into mid-May
plants.funFact: Wisteria twines in a set direction. Chinese wisteria winds counterclockwise, while Japanese wisteria (Wisteria floribunda) twists the opposite way, so you can tell the two apart from the vine alone.

plants.name: Paeonia officinalis
plants.description: This cottage-garden classic produces big, cup-shaped, fragrant crimson blooms with golden-yellow stamens at their centers. They sit above deeply cut green foliage on a compact, herbaceous clump. Peonies bring a rich, romantic splash of color at the point when spring tips into early summer.
plants.bloomingSeason: May (peony season runs from mid-May to late June)
plants.location: Native to Europe; blooming in temperate gardens of the northern United States and similar climates
plants.funFact: Ants swarm the sticky flower buds, but they are harmless. They simply feed on the sugary nectar the buds secrete, and a peony will open perfectly well without any help from them.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: As the Southern Hemisphere cools into autumn, this graceful evergreen shrub lights up with delicate, often lightly scented flowers. Its single or semi-double blooms open on glossy, dark green foliage, and the petals drift down like confetti beneath the bush.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-autumn through early winter in the Southern Hemisphere (roughly April to July)
plants.location: Gardens across southern Australia, where mid-May falls in autumn; native to China and Japan
plants.funFact: Sasanqua is one of the first camellias to bloom each year, and it is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant that gives us tea.
